Daily height loss is concrete, easy to check against your own body, and safe to share. It is also a new body topic that is not on the published list. topic: Daily height loss: spinal disc compression, overnight recovery, astronaut growth
hook: You're shorter tonight than this morning

slides.title: Blame your spine
slides.body: Soft discs sit between your vertebrae. All day, gravity slowly squeezes fluid out of them.
slides.image_prompt: Anatomical model of a human spine on a clean table, soft studio light, discs between vertebrae clearly visible

slides.title: The daily shrink
slides.body: Studies measuring adults morning and evening found they lose about 1% of their height by night.
slides.image_prompt: Vintage wooden height measuring ruler on a wall with a small marker sliding down, warm evening light

slides.title: Fastest after waking
slides.body: Most of the loss happens in the first hours after you get out of bed and start moving.
slides.image_prompt: Unmade bed in soft morning sunlight with an alarm clock on the nightstand, calm bedroom scene
slides.credit: Markus Spiske (CC0 / public domain) via openverse

slides.title: Sleep resets it
slides.body: Lying down takes the load off. Overnight, the discs soak fluid back up and you regain your height.
slides.image_prompt: Dark bedroom with moonlight across an empty bed, a sponge slowly absorbing water on the nightstand as a metaphor

slides.title: Astronauts grow
slides.body: With no gravity pressing down, the spine stretches out. Astronauts can grow up to 3% taller in space.
slides.image_prompt: Empty spacesuit floating inside a space station module with Earth visible through the window
slides.credit: NASA Johnson Space Center (Public domain) via wikimedia

cta: Part 2 tomorrow. Follow, don't miss it
caption:
You are not the same height you were this morning. Gravity squeezes fluid out of the discs in your spine all day. By evening, most adults are about 1% shorter, which is often 1 to 2 cm.

The good news is that you get it all back overnight while you sleep. In space there is no gravity to squeeze them, so astronauts come home up to 3% taller for a while (Spine journal, NASA).

Follow for one fact about your body you never noticed, every day. Would you measure yourself tonight to check?
